authority.name: City of Columbus Department of Building and Zoning Services

codeEdition.text: For one- to three-family houses Columbus enforces the 2019 Residential Code of Ohio together with the Columbus Building Code, and applies the 2023 National Electrical Code (NFPA 70) and the 2018 International Energy Conservation Code. Commercial and four-plus-family work falls under the 2024 Ohio Building, Plumbing and Mechanical Codes.

permitPolicy.text: An owner-occupant of a single-family house may apply for their own mechanical, electrical or plumbing permit by filing the city's homeowner affidavit. The affidavit requires a separate permit for each trade, names the person who will do the work, and bars contracting with an unlicensed contractor; it does not cover new single-family construction.

registration.text: Columbus requires a city license or registration on top of the state licence before a contractor can apply for a permit. Electrical and plumbing contractors must first hold an Ohio OCILB licence, then complete the city application, and anyone working as a journeyperson plumber needs a city-issued journeyperson plumber licence. The 2026 fee schedule lists a $300 new application fee, a $350 annual contractor licence and registration fee, and $150 annually for a journeyperson plumber.

codeItems.text: Water heater replacement is one of the few jobs Columbus puts on its Approved Minor Work Permit List, which is what lets it be permitted as a single-trade minor work permit with one inspection instead of a full mechanical/electrical/plumbing permit. Garbage disposals and standalone smoke detectors are not on that list.
A new or replacement backflow preventer or backwater valve is also on the Columbus minor work list, so it is permitted and inspected in its own right rather than folded into other plumbing work.

Ohio's residential code bars a fuel-fired water heater from a room used as a storage closet, and a water heater placed in a bedroom or bathroom must sit in a sealed enclosure so it does not draw combustion air from the living space. Direct-vent units are exempt from the enclosure.

Ohio rewrites the national GFCI rule for houses: it deletes NEC 210.8(D) (the dishwasher-outlet rule), exempts a single ceiling receptacle serving a garage door opener, and exempts a sump-pump receptacle when a GFCI duplex sits within six feet of the pump. It also exempts branch circuits serving only kitchen countertop receptacles from AFCI protection.

Ohio requires both photoelectric and ionization smoke-alarm technology on every level of a dwelling unit, using either separate alarms or dual-sensing units, which goes beyond the national model code.

water-heater-replacement.requirement: Replacing a water heater in Columbus needs a plumbing permit, and because the job is on the city's Approved Minor Work Permit List it is charged as a minor work permit that includes one inspection.
water-heater-replacement.fee: $140 Minor Work Permit - Electrical, Mechanical, or Plumbing only (1, 2 and 3 family dwellings, includes 1 inspection)

plumber-service-call.requirement: Plumbing work on a Columbus house that is not on the city's minor work list takes the standard mechanical, electrical and plumbing permit, which includes two inspections.
plumber-service-call.fee: $275 Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing permit (1, 2 and 3 family dwellings, includes 2 inspections); $140 if the job is on the Approved Minor Work Permit List

electrician-service-call.requirement: Electrical work on a Columbus house is permitted under the same mechanical, electrical and plumbing permit, with a cheaper single-trade minor work permit available only for jobs on the city's approved list.
electrician-service-call.fee: $275 Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing permit (1, 2 and 3 family dwellings, includes 2 inspections); $140 Minor Work Permit for electrical only if on the Approved Minor Work Permit List
